name: boundary
doc: A boundary (design/boundary.md): walls a playable region in so the player can't leave, while it looks like the world goes on. The game gives a hull (a config entry here: a predefined shape, or sectors by direction; a game gives its own cells) whose cells each name an edge (a ledge to look out from, a ridge's cliff, a mountain, a forest or jungle too thick to pass, a sea, a marsh) and a rise; rim resolves it into a smooth rim with the edges blended along it; terrain grows the world beyond it from those seeds out past the view distance, as a quadtree of terrain nodes with their own images that the runtime draws as a cut by distance, morphing between levels, with the rim's dressing and the walls that keep the player in. Trees and bushes within the figure range are figures: the game fills them from its own systems (the foundry with tree and bush).

params.name: hull
params.doc: The hull: one entry from config/boundary_hulls/ (a predefined shape, or sectors by direction around a ring); a game gives its own cells (foundry_boundary_spawn_hull).

params.name: biome
params.doc: The biome: its colours, tree forms, and scale.

params.name: detail
params.doc: How finely: the finest terrain spacing (2, 4, 8 m), the images (64, 32, 16 texels a node), and the dressing's density.

params.name: view_distance
params.doc: How far beyond the region the world reaches.

params.name: figure_range
params.doc: How far beyond the rim trees and bushes are figures for the game to fill from its own systems (design/boundary.md, Figures); past it the boundary draws its own woods. 0: it draws them all.

params.name: blend
params.doc: How far edges blend into each other along the rim.
